name: Jorabat–Zokhawthar Highway
aka: Formed from the former NH 40, NH 44, NH 154 and NH 54 (old numbering)
history: NH 6 is the main hill highway of the eastern side of Northeast India. It starts at Jorabat near Guwahati, climbs to Shillong, the capital of Meghalaya, drops into the Barak Valley of Assam, and then winds through the mountains of Mizoram past Aizawl all the way to Zokhawthar on the Myanmar border. It was created in the 2010 renumbering by joining several older highways, including the old NH 40 and NH 44.
facts: Runs through three states: Meghalaya, Assam and Mizoram.
The Jorabat–Shillong stretch is part of the international Asian Highway routes AH1 and AH2.
When first notified in 2010 it ended at Seling; it was later extended through Champhai to Zokhawthar on the Myanmar border.
One of the main road routes between the rest of India and Aizawl, the capital of Mizoram.
Was formed from the old NH 40, NH 44, NH 154 and NH 54.
